See also: мэл, мёл, and Appendix:Variations of "mel"

Bulgarian

[edit]

Pronunciation

[edit]
  • IPA(key): [mɛɫ]
  • Audio (Standard Bulgarian, l-vocalization):(file)
  • Rhymes: -ɛɫ

Etymology 1

[edit]

Inherited from Proto-Slavic *mělъ m.

Noun

[edit]

мел • (mel) m (dialectal)

  1. hillock, eminence, bank, cliff

[edit]

méla

References

[edit]
  • “мел¹”, in Речник на българския език [Dictionary of the Bulgarian Language] (in Bulgarian), Sofia: Bulgarian Academy of Sciences, 2014

Etymology 2

[edit]

Inherited from Proto-Slavic *mělь f.

Noun

[edit]

мел • (mel) f (dialectal)

  1. chalk, sandstone, limestone
    Synonyms: би́гор (bígor), варо́вик (varóvik)
  2. sludge, slurry, precipitation
    Synonym: ута́йка (utájka)
Declension
[edit]

mélite
Derived terms
[edit]
  • Мелник (Melnik, “Melnik”) (toponym)

References

[edit]
  • “мел²”, in Речник на българския език [Dictionary of the Bulgarian Language] (in Bulgarian), Sofia: Bulgarian Academy of Sciences, 2014
  • Georgiev, Vladimir I., editor (1986), “мел¹”, in Български етимологичен речник [Bulgarian Etymological Dictionary] (in Bulgarian), volume 3 (крес¹ – мѝнго¹), Sofia: Bulgarian Academy of Sciences Pubg. House, page 724

Etymology 3

[edit]

From Proto-Slavic *metlъ.

Participle

[edit]

мел • (mel)

  1. indefinite masculine singular past active aorist participle of мета́ (metá)

Pronoun

мел • (mel)

  1. how much

Komi-Zyrian

[edit]

Etymology

[edit]

Borrowed from Russian мел (mel).

Pronunciation

[edit]
  • IPA(key): /ˈmel/, [ˈmeɫ]
  • Hyphenation: мел

Noun

[edit]

мел • (mel)

  1. chalk

Mariupol Greek

[edit]

Etymology

[edit]

From Ancient Greek μέλι (méli). Cognates include Greek μέλι (méli).

Pronunciation

[edit]
  • IPA(key): [ˈmʲeɫ]
  • Hyphenation: мел

Noun

[edit]

мел • (mjel) n

  1. honey

Declension

[edit]
Declension of мел
singular plural
nominative мел (mjel) ме́ля (mjélja)
oblique мел (mjel) ме́ляс (mjéljas)

*) Some dialects don't use the oblique plural form, instead using the nominative plural.

References

[edit]
  • T. N. Chernysheva, editor (1859), “мел”, in Греческий глосарий Ф. А. Хартахая [The Greek glossary of F. A. Xartaxay], published 1959
  • A. A. Diamantopulo-Rionis with D. L. Demerdzhi, A. M. Davydova-Diamantopulo, A. A. Shapurma, R. S. Kharabadot, and D. K. Patricha (2006), “мел”, in Румейско-русский и русско-румейский словарь пяти диалектов греков Приазовья, Mariupol, →ISBN, page 130
  • G. A. Animica; M. P. Galikbarova (2013), Румеку глоса‎[1], Donetsk, page 83

Russian

[edit]
Russian Wikipedia has an article on:
мел
Wikipedia ru

Alternative forms

[edit]
  • мѣлъ (měl) — pre-1918 spelling

Etymology

[edit]

Inherited from Proto-Slavic *mělъ.

Pronunciation

[edit]
  • IPA(key): [mʲeɫ]
  • Audio:(file)
  • Audio (Saint Petersburg):(file)

Noun

[edit]

мел • (mel) m inan (genitive ме́ла, uncountable, relational adjective мелово́й)

  1. chalk
  2. (geology) Cretaceous
  3. (slang) cocaine

Declension

[edit]

nominative ме́л

mél

mélom

méle

mélu

melú

Derived terms

[edit]
  • мело́к m (melók)
  • мелова́ть impf (melovátʹ)
    • мелова́ние n (melovánije),
    • мело́ванный (melóvannyj)
    • размелова́ть pf (razmelovátʹ)
      • размело́ванный (razmelóvannyj)

Compounds:

  • беле́е ме́ла (beléje méla)
  • бле́дный как мел (blédnyj kak mel)
  • мелово́й пери́од m (melovój períod)

Related terms

[edit]
  • мо́лот m (mólot)
  • молоти́ть impf (molotítʹ)
  • моло́ть impf (molótʹ)

Descendants

[edit]
  • → Ingrian: mela
  • → Komi-Zyrian: мел (mel)
  • → Yakut: миэл (miel)
